summary: OWASP review of the session-authed API-key endpoint. Access control (requireOwned, uniform 404 anti-enumeration), hash-only storage (plaintext surfaced once via POST only, never persisted/logged), session-chain auth (403 anonymous, not shadowed by the key chain), and CSRF (session chain active) all verified. No findings requiring a fix.

findings.finding: Both GET and POST gate on requireOwned(ownerId, projectId, false) before any key read/write; foreign/missing/soft-deleted/malformed -> uniform 404; tests assert no key is created or exposed for non-owned projects.
findings.reason: Correct anti-IDOR / anti-enumeration. No change needed.

findings.finding: Plaintext key surfaced only in the POST response (ApiKeyGeneratedResponse); GET returns only the prefix mask; controller never logs plaintext/hash/prefix; hash-only at rest is enforced by ApiKeyService (Task 3) and asserted by the IT.

Endpoint on /api/v1/projects/** is served by the session chain (@Order(2)), not the /api/integrations/** key chain (@Order(1)); anonymous -> 403; currentUserId() fails closed on a malformed/absent principal. CSRF active on the session chain; POST IT uses csrf().
